Consult Summary:
- Five-day history of cough with runny nose, body aches, headaches, chills, and a dry hacking cough; no shortness of breath or wheeze; mild redness at the back of the throat; exam supports a viral upper respiratory infection.
- Managed with supportive care (OTC cough preparations: Night Nurse/Day Nurse); no antibiotics or new prescriptions. Chronic conditions include diabetes mellitus on metformin and hypertension on lisinopril with normal home BP monitoring. Reassurance given and follow-up advised if symptoms worsen or persist beyond 3 weeks.

- Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with cough

  - Systems review: no shortness of breath; no wheeze; no chest signs; throat: mild redness at back of throat; no enlarged tonsils; no cervical lymphadenopathy.
  - Medications/Examination findings: regular medications include metformin and lisinopril; no antibiotics prescribed; mouth exam noted.
  - Plan/differential: diagnosed as viral infection; advised symptomatic care; monitor for chest involvement or persistent symptoms.
